answer: A new agent starts in an open meadow of small tasks, not with full rights: it must build a behavioral fingerprint — timing, tool choices, error patterns — across many independently verified jobs over weeks, like copper threads woven through a canyon of records that cannot be copied or bought. Each extra identity costs another full, distinct history: about 60 hours of genuine, externally attested work a farm cannot parallelize without detection, because near-identical fingerprints collapse into one.
